anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The database simultaneously suffers from poorly written or overly heavy application SQL (SQL Workload Logic Anomaly), inaccurate or stale optimizer statistics (Optimizer Statistics Anomaly), and an excess buildup of obsolete MVCC row versions (MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly). Acting together, these three root causes drive the execution engine to read and process far more data than necessary, choose sub-optimal plans, and wade through bloated storage, all while background cleanup lags behind.  

Combined Observable Phenomena:  
• End-user transactions and reports show extreme and highly variable latency; many statements linger in slow-query logs with widening long-tail response times.  
• Execution plans reveal severe cardinality misestimates alongside scan-heavy or plan-flip behaviour; re-optimizations occur frequently yet fail to converge on efficient plans.  
• Buffer-pool hit ratios drop and I/O spikes as wide scans traverse pages full of dead or irrelevant rows; physical table and index sizes grow rapidly.  
• Locking is minimal, but snapshot/visibility checks escalate CPU usage; cleanup workers remain continuously active, and alerts about transaction-ID or version-store pressure appear.  
• Application-side retries and timeouts increase, sometimes masking as network or service failures, while DBA monitoring shows both statistics staleness warnings and vacuum/autovacuum backlog.  

Causal Interaction: Inefficient SQL causes large scans, large result sets, and long-running transactions that delay version reclamation, accelerating MVCC bloat. The expanding dead tuples, in turn, distort data distribution and row-count statistics, worsening the Optimizer Statistics Anomaly and leading the planner toward even poorer plans. Stale statistics further misguide the optimizer into full-table scans or wrong join orders, magnifying the overhead imposed by bloated heaps and indexes. The feedback loop between bad SQL logic, outdated statistics, and unchecked version buildup produces a self-reinforcing degradation cycle where each anomaly amplifies the others, rapidly eroding OLTP performance and stability.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits for additional data from a connection longer than net_read_timeout.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
